correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation gives u_prime=(1+sin t/4)e^{-t}>0 and u_doubleprime=e^{-2t}(-1+(cos t-sin t)/4)<0. Competitive equilibrium is unique by opposed demand/supply monotonicity, and θ(t)=lambda/min(exp(t)-1,1/lambda) decreases bijectively from infinity to zero. The binding condition rearranges exactly to sin t>4/(exp(t)-1). On each late positive-sine half-period h=sin t-4/(exp(t)-1) is strictly concave, has negative endpoints and positive midpoint, hence two and only two simple roots. Root distances from k pi are asymptotic to 4 exp(-k pi), and the exact clearing θ at equality is (exp(t)-1)^(-2); hence ratio exp(-2 pi). All boundary and strictness cases are handled. A standalone checker independently probes 75 finite equalities and inequalities; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result establishes genuinely unbounded budget active-set complexity within the exact positive-price, one-consumer market model under strict concavity, analytic utility and convex quadratic supply. The geometric threshold accumulation quantifies the difficulty near low production costs. It establishes a useful sharp limitation of finite-crossover simplifications beyond what correctness of the demand formula or ordinary convex optimization implies; no unsupported downstream applied guarantee is claimed.
